text:
maria: Heads-up — we've been seeing persistent AZ skew in gpu-nodepool-eu-prod. Autoscaler keeps spinning up GPUs in eu-west-1a and leaving b/c underpacked, then doesn't consolidate. Cost + capacity risk. Anyone seen this pattern?

aj: saw that last night in the dashboards. looks like burst workloads land in a single AZ then cooldown leaves free GPUs.

sean: is the expander set to least-waste or random? that can cause hotspotting.

maria: currently --expander=most-pods (default we rolled out). also have --balance-similar-node-groups=true but not sure it respects GPU taints.

rio: fwiw, CA ignores pod-affinity/anti-affinity sometimes when balancing. also if node creation time > max-provision-time, it won't consider alternatives.

aj: quick ideas: 1) try --expander=least-waste, 2) lower --scale-down-utilization-threshold for GPU pools to avoid premature scale-down, 3) enable --balance-similar-node-groups with stricter group labels.

sean: +1 on least-waste. also consider --skip-nodes-with-system-pods=false so we don't lock nodes because of hostpath/system pods. and bump --max-node-provision-time to 20m for spot interruptions.

maria: can we also stop scaling down GPU nodes if they've ever had a GPU pod in last 30m? we saw CA evict pods then nodes die and training restarts on different nodes with huge startup cost.

rio: you can annotate pods with cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=false but not great for long-term. alternate: mark GPU node groups with larger min-size or keep a small warm pool.

aj: propose a two-step canary: in eu-west-1a set --expander=least-waste + --scale-down-unneeded-time=15m for only gpu nodepools, monitor pod backfills and cost for 24h.

maria: okay I'll spin the canary on a single nodegroup tonight. can someone write the exact flags we should apply?

sean: suggested flags block (apply only to the CA deployment handling gpu pools):
```
--expander=least-waste
--scale-down-unneeded-time=15m
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.25
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false
--max-node-provision-time=20m
--ok-total-unready-count=5
```

aj: also add --expendable-pods-priority-cutoff=1000? that way low-priority batch jobs can be preempted for consolidation.

maria: noted. is there any risk this will force multi-AZ scheduling that violates our AZ affinity?

rio: least-waste prefers existing nodes that can fit pods instead of creating new ones, so it should reduce new nodes in the same AZ. balance-similar-node-groups helps spread across groups. but we should watch for increased scheduling latency.

autoscaler-bot: [alert] scale-down rejected for node gpu-pool-eu-1a-xyz: contains pods with PVCs (skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true)

sean: that alert explains previous failures — PVCs were blocking consolidation. we either need to migrate PVCs to shared storage or make CA ignore local storage for specific pools.

maria: I'll coordinate with storage on PVC migration for short-lived training artifacts. For now canary will include skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false for gpu pools.

aj: let's collect these metrics during the canary: per-AZ node count, pod pending times, preemptions, and cost per GPU-hour. if we see >10% increased pending or >5% cost uplift revert.

maria: sounds good. I'll create the canary PR and tag you all. planning to run for 48h, will roll back early if anything weird pops up. :thumbsup:

rio: thanks — also add a graph for "idle gpu-minutes" to the dashboard, that'll make the impact clear.

maria: will do. dropping notes in infra/runbooks after canary.
